---
title: "Reviewing survey studies for an ethics committee"
description: "Guidance for ethics committees: review the proposed questionnaire and study plan before collection, identify the submitted instrument version, then review the completed report and its recorded changes."
---

This page is for an ethics committee reviewing a survey study prepared with
surveyframe. You review the proposed documents before any responses are
collected, and the completed report with its recorded changes afterwards.

## Before collection: the proposed study

1. **Ask for the pre-analysis plan and the `.sframe` file.** The plan sets
   out the study, the participant information, the questionnaire and the
   planned analyses.
2. **Review the questionnaire.** The plan lists every question and the
   participant information. The researcher can also send the survey web page
   as a preview, so you see it as respondents will.
3. **Identify the submitted version.** The plan names the `.sframe` file's
   hash. Keep the file and the plan you approved with your decision.

## After the study: the completed report

1. **Check the version analysed.** The report's Provenance section names the
   questionnaire's hash. [Verify a `.sframe` file](https://surveyframe.org/verify/)
   to see whether it matches the version you approved.
2. **Review the recorded changes.** The Reproducibility section lists each
   amendment the researcher recorded, with its reason and date. Compare it
   with the version you approved to see what was disclosed.
